data.completion_memo: Implemented docs/subagent-tool-inheritance.md and audited against the native delegation design. Children receive exactly the delegating node's frozen selected tools (excluding recursive delegation), retain real broker/workspace/standing-grant enforcement, and return parent_approval_required with exact blocked actions without dispatch, child review calls, or later batch effects. Explicit readOnly filters native effect tools and requires both safe MCP hints regardless of auto-approve. Chat-owned jobs persist originating scope; children only control/complete their own jobs; parent and Stop supervise all Chat jobs. Child prompt/tool prefixes are stable across turns. Legacy frozen authority round-trips unchanged; pre-upgrade Settings remain valid; new Chats acquire the new contract. Native child span ancestry fixes live/replay attribution. Verification: cargo test --lib: 362 passed, 1 existing ignored local-capture fixture; 10 chat activity projection tests passed; tsc --noEmit passed; Vite production build passed; optimized executable built as desktop/src-tauri/target/release/aworkit-subagent-update.exe alongside the running original. Pipeline tests use real write/edit/shell/Python hosts, scripted MCP peer and model (no API spending), approval handoff/resume, replay and stable child prefixes; native job tests exercise sibling isolation and Chat cancellation. Existing user process was not restarted; no new live GUI session or paid provider run was used. git diff --check passed.
data.description: Implement docs/subagent-tool-inheritance.md and the linked native delegation contract. Preserve frozen legacy Chats, isolate per-node capabilities and child jobs, add readOnly selection, return approval-required work to parent without extra review LLM calls, and label child output correctly. Validate real writes and subprocess/job cancellation plus broker/MCP and UI projection regressions. Do not interrupt the user's active Chat.
data.title: Inherit parent tools for subagents with explicit approval handoff and actor ownership
